record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace R of L1[0,1] such that the quotient space L1[0,1]/R is isomorphic to L1[0,1]?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. ([37]) Does there exist an infinite dimensional reflexive subspace R of L1 such that L1/R isomorphic to L1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L^1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable real-valued functions on the unit interval, equipped with the norm $\|f\|_1 = \int_0^1 |f(t)|\,dt$. Recall that a Banach space $X$ is reflexive if the canonical embedding $X \hookrightarrow X^{**}$ is surjective, and two Banach spaces are said to be isomorphic if there exists a bounded linear bijection between them with bounded inverse.

Determine whether there exists an infinite-dimensional closed reflexive subspace $R \subset L^1[0,1]$ such that the quotient Banach space $L^1[0,1]/R$ is isomorphic to $L^1[0,1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether $L^1$ has an infinite-dimensional reflexive subspace with quotient isomorphic to $L^1$ is a known open problem in Banach space theory. Work by González and Martínez-Abejón on quotients of $L^1$ by reflexive subspaces addresses related structural questions but does not resolve this specific problem, and no published resolution was found in recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Quotients of L1 by reflexive subspaces
status_evidence.snippet: González and Martínez-Abejón study the structure of quotients of L1 by reflexive subspaces, presenting partial results without resolving the existence question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of reflexive subspaces R of L1 with L1/R isomorphic to L1 is studied but not resolved in available literature.

status_evidence.title: Some natural subspaces and quotient spaces of L1
status_evidence.snippet: The paper discusses natural subspaces and quotients of L1 but does not address or resolve the specific question.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the specific question is found in this related work.
